A_target.statement:
Let $K$ be [[Definition:Continuous Real Function|continuous]] on $\closedint a b^2$ and $g$ continuous on $\closedint a b$.
Let $\lambda \in \R$ with $\size \lambda \paren {b - a} \norm K_\infty < 1$.
Then the [[Definition:Fredholm Integral Equation|Fredholm integral equation]]:
:$\displaystyle \map f x = \map g x + \lambda \int_a^b \map K {x, y} \map f y \rd y$
has a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] continuous solution $f$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete metric space]] and $T: X \to X$ with $\map d {T x, T y} \le q \, \map d {x, y}$ for some $q < 1$.
Then $T$ has a unique [[Definition:Fixed Point|fixed point]].

substitutions.the complete metric space: C([a, b]) with the supremum metric
substitutions.the contraction T: f maps to g + lambda times the integral operator applied to f

derived.the fixed point: the solution of the integral equation

object_map.reformulation: Encode the integral equation as a fixed point equation for an affine integral operator.

validity_conditions: The smallness condition on lambda is what makes the operator a contraction.
C([a, b]) with the supremum norm is complete.
proof_plan:
Define $T$ on $\map C {\closedint a b}$ by:
:$\displaystyle \map {\paren {T f} } x = \map g x + \lambda \int_a^b \map K {x, y} \map f y \rd y$
$T f$ is continuous by uniform continuity of $K$.

For $f, h$:
:$
orm {T f - T h}_\infty \le \size \lambda \paren {b - a} 
orm K_\infty 
orm {f - h}_\infty = q 
orm {f - h}_\infty$
with $q < 1$.
By the [[Banach Fixed-Point Theorem]], $T$ has a unique fixed point $f$, which is the unique continuous solution.

Iterating from $f_0 = g$ expresses the solution as the [[Definition:Neumann Series|Neumann series]] $\displaystyle \sum_n \lambda^n \mathcal K^n g$, where $\mathcal K$ is the integral operator.
{{qed}}
